rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF ETHANOL AS ALTERNATIVE TRANSPORT FUEL, ESTABLISHING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL FUEL ETHANOL PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Seeks to establish petroleum independence due to the current trade imbalance by encouraging domestic production of ethanol fuels.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING CIVIL PENALTIES ON UNREASONABLE PRICE INCREASES FOR CRUDE OIL, RESIDUAL FUEL OIL, OR REFINED PETROLEUM PRODUCTS
rows.abstract: Imposes civil penalties to disproportionate and unjustified price increases of crude oil, residual oil, or refined petroleum products that are used as energy fuel in the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO MANDATE A COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH FOR THE PREVENTION, CONTROL, AND MEDICAL MANAGEMENT OF HEPATITIS C VIRUS INFECTION
rows.abstract: Expands efforts to uplift awareness of Hepatitis C Virus, and with this, strives to undertake increased medical research and heightened management to alleviate symptoms and infections.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PENAL CODE, ARTICLES 171 AND 172, IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR THE FALSIFICATION OF TORRENS CERTIFICATES OF TITLE
rows.abstract: Penalizes violators of the falsification of documents and certificates of title to a stricter degree as they scorn the instituted secure reputation of the Torrens System.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE ASSISTANCE FOR START-UP COSTS OF COMMUNITY PROGRAMS TO PREVENT RESIDENTIAL LEAD-BASED POISONING IN CHILDREN
rows.abstract: Seeks to provide protection of children to advocate for health consciousness as lead poisoning in residential homes has been a prevalent issue. Calls for startup costs to fund assistance from community programs to address and impede the harmful effects of lead poisoning especially to children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A WELFARE AND SOCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM TO   FAMILIES LEFT BEHIND BY OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.abstract: Prioritizes the families left by Overseas Filipino Workers by regarding their needs through welfare assistance and counseling services that seeks to address the issues linked to having a member of their family work overseas. Seeks to direct the OWWA to develop a clear  and comprehensive outline on the re-unification, reintegration, and re-placement scheme for returning OFWs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT ALL EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, WHETHER PUBLIC OR PRIVATE, SHALL HOLD MANDATORY CONSULTATION WITH STUDENTS, PARENTS OR GUARDIANS, ALUMNI, TEACHERS, AND OTHER NON-TEACHING PERSONNEL ASSOCIATIONS, BEFORE INCREASING AND/OR ADDING MISCELLANEOUS FEES, OTHER FEES, AND PAID SERVICES
rows.abstract: Seeks to provide that all educational institutions, whether public or private, shall hold mandatory consultation with their student councils/ governments, parents or guardians, alumni, faculty, and other non-teaching personnel associations, before increasing and/or adding miscellaneous fees, other fees, and paid services. In case no consensus is reached among the concerned educational institution and the concerned parties, the DepEd (for schools), CHED (for HEIs), or TESDA (Centers) is hereby authorized to decide in a summary proceeding whether the proposed increase or additional fee or paid services should be granted.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PENAL CODE, SECTION 248, TO DEFINE AND PENALIZE THE CRIME OF MURDER COMMITTED UNDER EXTRAORDINARY CIRCUMSTANCES
rows.abstract: Incorporates a subsection, Article 248-A, which expounds the definitions and penalties of murder committed under extraordinary circumstances.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PREVENT LUXURIOUS CONDITIONS IN PRISONS
rows.abstract: Prohibits prison officials to provide living conditions and opportunities  to  some prisoners that are more luxurious that those conditions and opportunities the average prisoner would have experienced.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PENAL CODE, ARTICLE 310, TO INCREASE THE PENALTIES IN CERTAIN INSTANCES OF QUALIFIED THEFT
rows.abstract:
Seeks to increase the penalties for the crime of theft on the following circumstances:
1.	The penalty of reclusion temporal in its maximum period to reclusion perpetua shall be imposed if the property taken on the occasion of the following: a. Fire, earthquake, typhoon, volcanic eruption, floods, or any other calamity natural or man-made; b. civil disruption or disturbance, public want or emergency; and c. accidents involving land, sea, air and transport.
2.	The penalty of reclusion perpetua shall be imposed if the offender is a law enforcement agent or officer, a barangay official, a fireman of the Bureau of Fire Protection and of other civil organization exercising the same functions, and any other government official or employee entrusted with a duty to render assistance on the foregoing occurrences.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 386, ALSO KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, ARTICLE 1032, ON UNWORTHINESS TO SUCCEED
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the issue that disqualification to succeed by reason of unworthiness is gender-biased:
               “(1) Parents who have abandoned their children or induced their daughters to 
   lead a corrupt or immoral life, or attempted against their virtue . . .”

Proposes to include parents who induce their sons to lead corrupt or immoral lives among the people incapable of succeeding because of unworthiness.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING  ACT  NO.  7160  ALSO  KNOWN  AS  THE  LOCAL  GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, SECTION 17 (B), PARAGRAPH 1(V), ON THE OBLIGATION OF LOCAL  GOVERNMENT  UNITS  TO  MAINTAIN  BARANGAY  ROADS,  BRIDGES AND WATER SUPPLY SYSTEMS
rows.abstract: Repeals the obligation of local government units to maintain barangay roads, bridges, and water supply systems and return it to the obligation of the national government as there are some barangays in need of extensive repair and maintenance that exceeds the funds that the LGUs are provided with by the Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE OFFICE OF RESEARCH ON WOMEN´S HEALTH
rows.title_short: Intends To Conduct Research On Women´s Health Which Shall Be Responsive To The Needs Of Every Woman.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR RESTRICTIONS ON GARNISHMENT OF COMPENSATION DUE FOR PERSONAL SERVICES
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO CONDUCT A FEASIBILITY STUDY FOR APPLYING AIRPORT BUBBLES AS A METHOD OF IDENTIFYING, ASSESSING, AND REDUCING THE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF THE AIRPORT GROUND AND FLIGHT OPERATIONS AND IMPROVING THE OVERALL QUALITY OF THE ENVIRONMENT
rows.abstract:
Requires the Secretary of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources to conduct a feasibility study for applying airport bubbles in preventing detrimental effects of flight operations and pollution to the environment. 
Defines “Airport bubble” as an area 1.) in and around an airport, or other facility using aircraft, within which sources of pollution and level of pollution from those sources are to be identified and reduced and; 2.) containing a variety of types of air, noise, water, and solid waste sources of pollution in which the aggregate of each type of pollutant from the respective sources is regulated as if the various sources were single source.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE GRANTS TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS   FOR SUPERVISED VISITATION CENTERS
rows.abstract: Aims to protect the children of separated parents from witnessing violent acts by their parents during visitation or exchanges by having them supervised by local government units to ensure a safe and guarded environment for all the members of the family.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPROVE THE SAFETY OF NON-MOTORIZED TRANSPORTATION, INCLUDING PEDESTRIAN AND BICYCLE SAFETY, IN THE VICINITY OF SCHOOLS
rows.abstract: Integrates non-motorized means of transport into the country´s traffic scheme. Directs the Department of Transportation to develop a comprehensive plan and program to ensure the safety of pedestrian, bicycle, and other non-motorized transportation focusing on the vicinity of schools.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF DRUG AND ALCOHOL ABUSE AMONG HIGH RISK YOUTH
rows.abstract:
Defines “High-Risk Youth” by enumerating certain youth groups more vulnerable or susceptible to substance abuse who may not have any access to formal institutional structures due to their marginalized status.

Mandates DOH to make priority grants that would assist public and nonprofit entities for their community-based programs or projects that intend to develop and demonstrate innovative and effective models with multiple, coordinated services and which employ research designs so that disenfranchised sectors of the youth may be saved from the debilitating effects of substance abuse and become competent partners in development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO EMPOWER THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION (DEPED), THE   COMMISSION ON HIGHER EDUCATION (CHED), AND THE TECHNICAL   EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (TESDA) TO REQUIRE   ALL THE SCHOOL HEADS TO REPORT ALL THE INCIDENTS OF STUDENT   SUICIDE IN THEIR RESPECTIVE SCHOOLS, WHETHER CONSUMMATED,   FRUSTRATED, OR ATTEMPTED, AND TO PROVIDE A PROGRAM FOR STUDENT SUICIDE EARLY INTERVENTION AND PREVENTION
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the absence of concrete steps in determining the causes of suicide among the Filipino youth and to raise awareness of student suicide as a serious public health program.
Proposes to establish a Task Force which shall collect information; study, make findings, conclusions, and recommendations regarding that information; and submit reports to Congress and also to the Civil Registrar a database regarding the incidence of student suicides.
Provides several strategies that are fair, prompt, timely, continuous, up-to-date, appropriate, and effective to assist schools in achieving suicide reduction targets.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO SUPPORT BUSINESS INCUBATION IN ACADEMIC SETTINGS
rows.abstract:
Defines “incubator” as an entity affiliated with or house in a degree-granting institution that provides space and coordinated and specialized services to entrepreneurial businesses which meet selected criteria during the businesses´ start-up phase.
Proposes to authorize CHED:  to support the establishment and development of incubators; to allocate funds to make awards on a competitive basis to support the program and funds for research regarding best practices; to contract with organizations with expertise in business incubation practices; and to identify specified recipients of such awards.
Provides that CHED shall give priority to funding applications that provide strong educational opportunities to students in entrepreneurship, and that require significant collaboration between businesses, academia, and local government and economic development leaders.
rows.alias_name: "Linking Educators and Developing Entrepreneurs for Reaching Success (LEADERS) Act"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH THERAPEUTIC EQUIVALENCE REQUIREMENTS   FOR GENERIC DRUGS
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others such as “Essential Drugs List” or “National Drug Formulary”; “Core List”; and “Complementary List”
Intends to ensure that the drug products with similar generic name also contain the same chemical components responsible for the claimed therapeutic effects.
Enumerates several requirements for a drug to be considered the therapeutic equivalent of a drug listed in the Essential Drugs List or National Drug Formulary before its approval by the DOH Secretary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR UNIFORM WARNINGS ON PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT FOR OCCUPATIONAL USE
rows.abstract:
Intends to enhance understanding of the proper use and limits of PPEs through safety warning and health standards to reduce injuries and illnesses resulting from their faulty use.
Prescribes certain standard warnings for the manufacturer or other seller which shall be communicated to the employer using PPEs, and for the employer to communicate to each employee using the same; and to train, educate and instruct such employees as regards to PPEs proper use, warning vis-Ã -vis workplace and work environment; and consequences of failing to observe each warning.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE TRAINING ON VIOLENCE PREVENTION TO PROFESSIONALS WHO WORK WITH CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
Proposes a program that: 1) trains and provides professional development to individuals working in early child development programs or elementary schools; and 2) provides training to become an early childhood education/school teacher, counselor, or care provider. 
Intends to give priority to award grants with approved application to carry out violence prevention programs that include one or more components as regards to engaging family support and community outreach or collaboration with other services in the community, conflict resolution training with at-risk children, working in and with - economically disadvantaged communities/students, and carrying out training programs with proven effectiveness.
rows.alias_name: “Violence Prevention Training for Early Childhood Educators Act”
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A NATIONAL PROGRAM THAT WILL PROVIDE PREGNANT WOMEN WITH ALTERNATIVES TO ABORTION
rows.abstract: Seeks to establish a national program that will:  promote childbirth as a viable and positive alternative to abortion and empower those facing unplanned or crisis pregnancies to choose childbirth rather than abortion; support entities and projects that provide information, counseling, and support services that assist women to choose childbirth and to make informed decisions regarding the choice of adoption or parenting with respect to their children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2021-03-25

rows.author: I051
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2021-11-29, transmitted to the Senate on 2021-12-01 and received by the Senate on 2021-12-01
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRARIAN REFORM AND THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE TO SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO CONGRESS ON STATISTICS RELATING TO THE CONVERSION OF AGRICULTURAL LAND TO NON-AGRICULTURAL USES INCLUDING A REVIEW OF EXISTING POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the continued decrease of the country´s agricultural land base which threatens its ability to produce sufficient food to meet domestic needs, and undermines the economic base of many rural areas.
Proposes to develop criteria to identify the effects of government programs on agricultural land conversion; tasks the department agencies and LGUs to use such criteria to determine and take into account its adverse effects on said land preservation; consider appropriate alternative actions that could lessen such adverse effects; and evaluation of said programs and policies´ compatibility with the development plans at the national and local levels.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10303

rows.author: J071
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING ENTERPRISE-BASED EDUCATION AND TRAINING, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Aims to address gaps leading to jobs-skill mismatch in order to tap the full productive potential of the labor force especially college graduates.
Defines Enterprise-Based Education and Training programs (EBET) to practical training programs with compulsory related theoretical instructions conducted on/off-the-job being implemented within companies.
Intends to enhance the skills of the middle-level workforce by strengthening the participation of the private sector in Technical-Vocational Education and Training (TVET) - to empower more companies, organizations, and other institutions to offer enterprise-based training programs compliant to standards which shall be formulated by TESDA.
Proposes to establish a national enterprise-based training system and standards which shall ensure that the student/trainees will acquire the right competencies in an environment where their rights and safety are protected.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2021-03-25

rows.author: J071
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE TELECOMMUTING ACT AND PROVIDING INCENTIVES FOR TELECOMMUTING EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE, REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11165, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TELECOMMUTING ACT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to expand R.A. 11165 to include in its coverage institutions from the PUBLIC sector and to provide incentives of a non-taxable telecommuting allowance of at least ONE THOUSAND PESOS (P1,000.00) for every month served under telecommuting agreement.
Provides that existing similar benefits shall not be eliminated or reduced upon implementation of this proposed law and there shall be no prohibition for employers or the Collective Bargaining Agreement to offer higher or more favorable terms than what was provided in this Act.
Proposes further that telecommuting allowances granted by private employers shall be deductible for income tax purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: J071
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF THE MUNICIPAL GENERAL SERVICES OFFICER IN MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AMENDING SECTION 443 (a) AND SECTION 490 (a) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract:
Intends to effectively guarantees the uniformity of general services management of the local government units in the provincial, city and MUNICIPAL level.
Seeks to ensure the speedy delivery of services requiring general services expertise and technical support services which shall likewise provide for an improved system of procurement, care, utilization, custody, and disposal of supplies or properties of the LGU.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2021-03-25

rows.author: J071
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7925, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATIONS POLICY ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES", BY REQUIRING PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATIONS ENTITIES AND INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS TO INSTITUTE A REFUND MECHANISM FOR SERVICE OUTAGES AND DISRUPTIONS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the poor quality of internet and cellular connectivity services offered by TelCos/ISPs which are riddled with service outages, disruptions, and interruptions.
Proposes to provide on a pro-rated basis, a refund credit or a bill adjustment to a customer who has experienced a service outage or disruption for an aggregate period of twenty-four (24) hours or more within a month.
Provides that such refund credit or bill adjustment shall be granted to customers subscribing to a service on a pre-paid basis who need not take any action in order to receive a refund.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2021-03-25

rows.author: J071
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE YOUTH SUICIDE INTERVENTION AND PREVENTION
rows.abstract:
Seeks to:  include Life Planning course in the elementary and secondary education curriculum; implement a peer counseling group program; conduct a nationwide public education suicide awareness campaign; employ at least one psychologist in every school for monthly counseling alignment sessions; to establish a network of health facilities and teen centers to address identified youth issues.
Provides that Life Planning Education (LPE) shall require lectures and discussions on self and identity; personal, family, community values; communication and interrelationship with others; sexuality and gender roles; community participation; health; psychological thinking and employment, among others.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2021-03-25

rows.author: J015
rows.title_full: AN ACT  IMPROVING  TEACHER  QUALITY  THROUGH  THE  ESTABLISHMENT  OF  A TEACHER EDUCATION FOR ACHIEVERS PROGRAM, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to uplift the teaching profession's image and encourage and attract the best and brightest to teach by strengthening the enrollment requirements and providing merit-based scholarships for students entering pre-service teacher training institutions.
Proposes to establish Teacher Education Council and Centers of Excellence to produce high-quality teachers and improve the quality of learning outcomes through policies and practices where pre-service and in-service teacher education is prioritized.
Aims to ensure that future teachers are classroom-ready and contributors to improved learning outcomes by providing the best training, full financial and psychosocial support, and employment assistance.
Proposes to provide holistic support for the teacher grantees such as scholarship package; continuous mentorship and training and development; teaching position upon graduation; and other various incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2021-03-25

rows.author: G097
rows.title_full:
AN ACT
REGULATING THE PRODUCTION, IMPORTATION, SALE, DISTRIBUTION, PROVISION, USE, RECOVERY, COLLECTION, RECYCLING, AND DISPOSAL OF SINGLE-USE PLASTIC PRODUCTS
rows.title_short: Single- Use Plastic Products Regulation Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to impose a ban on the production, importation, sale, provision and use of single-use plastics to curb the growing problem of plastic pollution in the country.

Provides for a gradual phase out of single-use plastic products, a program for the shift to the use of biodegradable plastics, encouragement of the use of reusable, recyclable, and retrievable products, a recovery program for the significant reduction in consumption and  increased recovery for recycling and treatment, or proper disposal of single-use plastic products,  the role of local government units, penalties for violators, a program for affected workers of the plastic industry and support for affected manufacturers of plastic products, among others.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2021-07-28, transmitted to the Senate on 2021-07-29 and received by the Senate on 2021-07-29

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING HATE SPEECH AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Anti-hate Speech Act
rows.abstract:
Defines “Hate Speech” as all forms of expressions, including advocacy, that constitute incitement to discrimination, hostility and violence against any person or group of persons on the basis of ethnicity, race, religion, color, national or social origin, birth, indigenous origin or identity, migrant or refugee status, political or other opinion, sexual orientation, gender identity, sex language, and disability.

Prohibits the following acts when containing hate speech: a.) Utterance or writing words, or displays or depiction of behavior made before a public audience; b.) Publication or distribution of written material to the public or through social media, broadcasting or other forms of communications; or c.) Public performance of plays, shows, recordings of audio or visual images.

Penalizes any person violating any provision of this Act by arresto mayor or imprisonment for a period of not less than thirty (30) days or not more than six (6) months and/or a fine of not less than Ten thousand pesos (Php 10,000.00) or more than One hundred thousand pesos (Php100,000.00), and non-custodial sanctions such as community service, taking into consideration the circumstances and gravity of the offense.
